ai.description: *Beddomixalus bijui* is a slender, 4–5 cm frog with a pale brown dorsum featuring two distinct, thin, cream-colored dorsolateral stripes. It possesses a pointed snout and lacks webbing on the fingers.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Beddomixalus bijui* is best distinguished by the prominent, creamy-white longitudinal stripe running along its entire flank, which is absent in other similar Indian tree frogs.
ai.habitat: *Beddomixalus bijui* inhabits evergreen forests and riparian zones in the Western Ghats, typically found at mid-to-high altitudes ranging from 800 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Beddomixalus bijui* is primarily nocturnal and constructs unique foam nests above water bodies, where its larvae develop after hatching and dropping into the pool below.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Beddomixalus bijui* breeds during the monsoon, depositing foam nests containing 100–150 eggs on vegetation overhanging water, into which tadpoles drop upon hatching.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Beddomixalus bijui* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests in Kerala and Tamil Nadu above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Beddomixalus bijui* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation near montane forest streams.
